chapter: Lucky Roberts, Armstrong and the big-band rivalries
title: Playing society estates and yachts for Lucky Roberts
summary: The nine-piece band played teas, dances and regattas on millionaires' estates, with members singing, plus anecdotes about a drunk trombonist and Lucky's 'demon' talk.

bands.name: Cozy Cole and his Red Hot Cinders

story.theme_name: Getting paid: wages, tips and leaving over money
story.community_name: Dance halls, lake resorts and where bands played

blocks.x: Now, when you were working with these personnel, were they private parties you were playing like for the Whigbys[ble].

(Inaudible) he would give a reception ---these were or something for this bunch of people /millionaires. Sometimes they would call them teas. He'd give it all out on the estate, everything, cricket and croquet and all that stuff. And we'd come in, you'd have tea and sherbert (inaudible). And then you would relax to you would like to do, play cricket or croquet or whatever you were doing. Then have dinner, played (inaudible) various pretty things, sing a little bit. And then about 11:00 o'clock, after the dance -- or it may last for a whole week. And sometimes they had the regatta. They had their yachts. Or if you feel like going to Bermuda (inaudible). That was it.
How many people were in the band?
Well, there was about nine. And then he would break them up in units. If there was no use for the trumpet, he didn't call for a trumpet or muted trumpet, you
had to sing. And when he had to get the loud thing he used the trumpet.

Once he took one trombone player with him, and the trombone player got very inebriated and had one of those big, pretty naps. Had one of those beautiful lamps, he had it in his pants, taking it out. And his excuse was, 'Oh, I was drunk, I didn't know what I was doing.' And Lucky said, yes, but I was aware. It's unfortunate. Most unfortunate. That was the end of that.

And Lucky's words for a musician, he'd call you 'Demon,' 'hello, Demon.' Because that's another way to call them so and so and his jazz demons. One of these, they had (inaudible) little devils--imps, behind the music. Because Cozy Coles had a band and they had him back there with horns and they had (inaudible), and had imps all around him. But that didn't move me too much.
Cozy Cole and his Red Hot Cinders.
